title: Tanker Strikes Docked Riverboat in New Orleans; All Aboard Accounted For After Capsizing
dek: A tanker struck the docked American Heritage riverboat on the Mississippi in New Orleans on Friday and it capsized; officials say everyone aboard was accounted for.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The Crescent City Queen riverboat docked at New Orleans in a 1996 photo (file image, not the American Heritage)

keyPoints: A tanker, the Atlantic Asphalt, struck the American Heritage riverboat while it was docked near the French Quarter at about 12:30 p.m. local time Friday, officials said.
The riverboat listed, then flipped; passengers and crew ended up in the Mississippi. Officials said everyone aboard was accounted for.
Mayor Helena Moreno said 32 passengers were hospitalized with non-critical injuries; Fox 10 reported 30 passengers and two harbor police officers.
Officials gave different counts of people aboard, from about 180 to 197.
The Coast Guard said the tanker appeared to have lost steering; the cause is unknown. The NTSB is sending investigators.
body:
The American Heritage, a riverboat operated by American Cruise Lines, was docked in the Port of New Orleans near the French Quarter on Friday when the tanker Atlantic Asphalt struck it, [NBC News reported](https://nbcnews.com/news/us-news/rescue-underway-oil-tanker-collides-new-orleans-river-boat-rcna609235). Officials said the collision happened at about 12:30 p.m. local time, and that the boat began to sink and flipped while passengers were still disembarking, Mayor Helena Moreno said.

Workers aboard told [Fox 10](https://fox10tv.com/2026/11/13/everyone-aboard-american-heritage-riverboat-all-rescuers-survived-collision-with-tanker) that the impact shattered windows, that the restaurant filled with knee-deep water within seconds, and that they escaped through an emergency exit, swam to the wharf and climbed ladders and ropes dropped from above.

## A rescue officials called a miracle

Moreno called the outcome “a miracle on the Mississippi” and said officials had zero people unaccounted for, [ABC13 reported](https://abc13.com/story/emergency-crews-responding-vessel-collision-port-new-orleans-mississippi-river/20038750/). Fox 10 reported that it took nearly 45 minutes to get everyone out of the river and onto dry land. Port employees ran to the water and threw life preservers, a Regional Transit Authority ferry pulled one survivor to safety, and other nearby vessels also responded, the station reported.

A New Orleans firefighters’ union official told Fox 10 that firefighters on the riverboat were helping people off when the boat began to list. Firefighters on shore removed ladders to keep people from jumping onto them, and those on board grabbed railings and pulled nearby people in as the boat tipped over.

## Counts differ across outlets

Early figures for the number of people aboard vary. NBC News reported Moreno’s estimate of between 180 and 190 people. [CNN reported](https://edition.cnn.com/2026/11/13/us/new-orleans-tanker-crash) that all 197 passengers made it to safety, while Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry hailed the rescue as a “miracle on the Mississippi.” Fox 10 reported that first reports put about 129 passengers aboard at the time of impact, and that more than 100 people were still on board when the boat capsized.

Injury figures are closer. CNN and NBC both reported that Moreno said 32 passengers were taken to hospitals with non-critical injuries. Fox 10 reported 30 people and two harbor police officers in the hospital. Meridian is reporting the ranges because the officials’ counts have not been reconciled.

## Investigation

The U.S. Coast Guard and the National Transportation Safety Board are investigating. Coast Guard Capt. Melanie Burnham said the tanker appeared to have had “some type of a loss of steering,” but that officials did not know why, [ABC13 reported](https://abc13.com/story/emergency-crews-responding-vessel-collision-port-new-orleans-mississippi-river/20038750/). Burnham said the cruise boat was “significantly damaged.” ABC13 also reported that the NTSB was launching a team expected on scene Saturday morning, and that American Cruise Lines confirmed the riverboat was involved.

NBC News reported that the federal transportation officials who would lead the probe were delayed in reaching New Orleans by the nationwide FAA ground stop on Friday. Meridian’s separate story on that stop is linked here: [FAA nationwide ground stop lifted](/article/faa-nationwide-ground-stop-telecom-outage-lifted-friday).

## What is not yet known

The reporting reviewed for this story does not establish why the tanker lost steering, what the investigators will conclude, or whether any party will face action. Meridian will update this story if the Coast Guard or the NTSB release findings.
